findings.summary: _quote escapes a quote character inside a table name with a backslash, which SQL identifiers do not support, so a table name containing a double quote breaks or rewrites every statement.
archive(dry_run=True) creates the archive table before it returns the count, so a dry run changes the database.
Each batch is selected with an offset of the rows already moved, but moved rows are deleted, so later batches skip rows and they are never archived.
The default archive table name is built from the model's class name instead of its table name, so a model with a custom table_name gets a wrongly named archive.
count() creates the archive table when it does not exist instead of returning 0, so reading the count changes the database, even right after a dry run or against a read-only connection.
